prompt:
Use case: illustration-story, precise reference-guided revision.
Create ONE beautiful horizontal 16:9 cinematic watercolor comic opening concept by revising Image 1 to address THREE specific corrections: (1) MUCH MORE STAGGERED, ANGULAR, IRREGULAR zigzag panel geometry, (2) all depictions of the entrance must match the SAME simple straight gate from Image 3, (3) final panel must be a NEW NARRATIVE CAMERA SHOT of arriving in the garden, NOT a reproduction of the first-level screen.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1: previous comic to revise. Retain excellent watercolor character rendering, wide pale parchment spaces, soft warm/cool colors and subtle ink lines. REPLACE its regular top-row/bottom-panorama layout, REPLACE its incorrect fancy arched gate, REPLACE the level-map last panel.
Image 2: polygon layout reference only. Use its bold staggered angles, off-center diagonal joins and irregular varying-size shapes, reimagined for HORIZONTAL widescreen. Do not copy its portrait orientation or black/white style, or any text.
Image 3: exact architectural continuity guide, NOT final-panel composition. Use ONLY the specific gate construction, brick-and-plaster wall materials, giant ivy/tree canopy, damp mossy stone threshold and antique garden mood. Do NOT paste the gameplay scene into any panel. Do not reproduce its props in a complete left-to-right line.
Image 4: authoritative protagonist identity reference.

PAGE AND COMIC GEOMETRY, CRITICAL:
Landscape 16:9 single aged storybook parchment sheet, NOT two pages. Fine warm ivory/oatmeal vellum fibers, faint tasteful age spots near edges, no burnt edges or scroll rolls or book spine. Wide uncovered parchment gutters about 2.5 to 3 percent of overall image width, and outer margins about 3 percent. Thin single sepia panel outlines. All polygon corners remain separated by clearly visible parchment.
Exactly FIVE boldly unequal polygon panels with diverse diagonal angles and an unmistakable ZIGZAG main dividing ribbon. Do NOT use four regular top tiles above a giant bottom rectangle. Do NOT make equally wide stripes. Do NOT align the junctions into a clean rectangular grid. Avoid repeated parallel cuts.
Use this logical polygon arrangement as a geometric guide (coordinates normalized to the inner artwork area before adding wide parchment gutters):
Panel 1 upper-left polygon: (0,0), (34,0), (30,46), (0,62).
Panel 2 upper-middle pentagon: (34,0), (68,0), (72,36), (48,61), (30,46).
Panel 3 upper-right polygon: (68,0), (100,0), (100,52), (72,36).
Panel 4 lower-left pentagon: (0,62), (30,46), (48,61), (40,100), (0,100).
Panel 5 lower-right pentagon: (48,61), (72,36), (100,52), (100,100), (40,100).
Inset EACH polygon to leave VERY WIDE natural paper gaps between them; coordinates are a starting topology, not printed graphics. The major parchment channel visibly steps up, down, up, down across the page, creating several distinct sharp bends and T junctions at DIFFERENT heights. Three upper story beats, two lower story beats, but strongly staggered irregular polygon silhouettes instead of two straight rows. Final lower-right panel largest about 30 percent, NOT a full-width panoramic strip. Every illustration upright; slanted panel borders, not tilted horizons.

NARRATIVE READING:
PANEL 1, upper left: wide side view of tiny spirit walking right along the abandoned old mossy wall, dark big ivy overhead and storm-blue dusk sky. Quiet loneliness before a storm.
PANEL 2, upper middle: close/mid shot of spirit parting or looking past enormous leaves, its face turned right with tentative hope, a distant little amber reflection visible on greenhouse glass through a leaf gap. Greenhouse is distant and small, the light ambiguous, NOT a literal person or flame.
PANEL 3, upper right: low view from OUTSIDE of the simple SAME straight garden gate from Image 3. Tiny spirit reaches the foot of its pale square masonry pier. Gate towers above it. Gate is rectangular and its top rail horizontal, spear finials on straight vertical bars, NOT an arched palace gate.
PANEL 4, lower left: intimate low macro view of the SAME gate's base: a pale stone threshold, dark straight bars, rust at bottom rail, ivy and loose moss; tiny spirit carefully steps through an existing ground-level gap. Show the feet crossing the worn threshold. The geometry of bars and stone pier stays identical to panel 3. No exaggerated open giant ornate doors.
PANEL 5, lower right: NEW cinematic NARRATIVE SHOT, from a few centimeters above the ground just inside the threshold, three-quarter rear view of tiny spirit standing on moss and looking right into an empty overgrown garden. It has just realized nobody is tending the place. A cropped section of the same straight black iron gate and pale square pier provides a dark framing edge at LEFT; big ivy leaves canopy over it. In front of the tiny spirit are damp moss tufts, a few fallen leaves and small rubble; behind them a portion of the reference's aging red-brick/cream-plaster garden wall recedes obliquely into cool dim atmospheric depth. A cropped edge of the old chipped terra-cotta pot may sit at the far right in shade as a quiet shared landmark, but no staged row of gameplay props. The close threshold and receding wall define the shot, NOT a wide survey of the level. No full mirror-puzzle tableau, no scale-shaped mound reveal, no complete level platform, no level screenshot, no diagram of the route. Never reuse the previous last image. This is emotional arrival and discovery; gentle uncertainty in posture, vast unused space beyond at the spirit's scale. A very small residual warm dusk glow catches nearby moss and brick edges, while the garden beyond remains cool and deserted. Match-cut visual anchors into later gameplay: gate bars, square pier, ivory/red wall, ivy and moss ground, not identical camera composition.

ABSOLUTE GATE DESIGN LOCK:
The gate in Image 3 is a simple old black/brown wrought-iron rectangular garden gate with mostly parallel STRAIGHT VERTICAL bars and small spear-shaped finials, straight horizontal rails and only MODEST small curls immediately under the top rail. Its silhouette is almost FLAT/HORIZONTAL at the top. Pale cream square stone pillar with a low red-brick cap. Do not use the grand ornate twin-leaf ARCHED gate seen in Image 1; remove that design completely from every panel. No fan, circle, large scrolls, oval center, tall central arch, gothic arch or palace portal. The same scale, material and rail spacing across panels 3, 4 and the edge of 5. Panel 4 must feature straight bars and base rail, not a swirling metal arch.

CHARACTER:
Faithfully preserve Image 4: creamy ivory flame-shaped enormous head sweeping back, two simple black vertical oval eyes, tiny mouth, short chubby torso and limbs, small golden leaf/flame chest inset. Blue-gray watercolor shadow patches, little luminous tips and sparse embers. No clothes, no bag, no umbrella, no props, no horns/ears/wings. Thumb-sized, a large ivy leaf is bigger than its head, a human gate is vastly taller. Do not resize the spirit to child-sized. One spirit per panel, the same character across the five panels.

STYLE / ATMOSPHERE:
Refined hand-painted watercolor and thin ink contours, subtle granulated paper, faded moss greens and gray-blue dusk with restrained honey-amber highlights. Layered foliage silhouettes and depth inspired by LIMBO, delicate architectural illustrated detail inspired by Gorogoa. Keep environment material continuity with Image 3 while using cool twilight before rain, not golden noon. NO rain streaks, storm has not started. No added people, monster, light beams, magic attacks, activated mechanisms, dialogue, lettering, panel numbering, arrows, labels, watermarks or UI. No character or prop crosses a gutter. Final image should read as an evocative irregular comic page painted on aged parchment, NOT a level concept sheet.
